label: def:generalized-closed-sets
title: Definition
body_md:
\label{def:generalized-closed-sets}
Let $\mathbb{A}\subseteq\mathbb{X}$. Then $\mathbb{A}$ is said to be:
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)]

    \item \emph{regular-closed} \cite{stone1937applications} if
    \[
    \mathbb{A}
    =
    \operatorname{cl}
    \bigl(\operatorname{int}(\mathbb{A})\bigr);
    \]

    \item \emph{semi-closed} \cite{levine1963semi} if
    \[
    \operatorname{int}
    \bigl(\operatorname{cl}(\mathbb{A})\bigr)
    \subseteq \mathbb{A};
    \]

    \item \emph{$w$-closed} \cite{Sundaram2000} if
    \[
    \operatorname{cl}(\mathbb{A})\subseteq\mathbb{U},
    \]
    whenever $\mathbb{A}\subseteq\mathbb{U}$ and
    $\mathbb{U}$ is semi-open in $\mathbb{X}$;

    \item \emph{$\alpha$-closed} \cite{njȧstad1965some} if
    \[
    \operatorname{cl}
    \bigl(
        \operatorname{int}
        (\operatorname{cl}(\mathbb{A}))
    \bigr)
    \subseteq\mathbb{A};
    \]

    \item an \emph{$\alpha^{*}$-set} \cite{hatir1996decomposition} if
    \[
    \operatorname{int}
    \bigl(
        \operatorname{cl}
        (\operatorname{int}(\mathbb{A}))
    \bigr)
    =
    \operatorname{int}(\mathbb{A});
    \]

    \item a \emph{$C$-set} \cite{hatir1996decomposition} if
    \[
    \mathbb{A}=\mathbb{U}\cap\mathbb{V},
    \]
    where $\mathbb{U}$ is open and $\mathbb{V}$ is an
    $\alpha^{*}$-set in $\mathbb{X}$;

    \item \emph{$h$-closed} \cite{rodrigo2012international} if
    \[
    s\text{-}\operatorname{cl}(\mathbb{A})
    \subseteq\mathbb{U},
    \]
    whenever $\mathbb{A}\subseteq\mathbb{U}$ and
    $\mathbb{U}$ is $w$-open in $\mathbb{X}$;

    \item \emph{$gh$-closed} \cite{rodrigo2012international} if
    \[
    h\text{-}\operatorname{cl}(\mathbb{A})
    \subseteq\mathbb{U},
    \]
    whenever $\mathbb{A}\subseteq\mathbb{U}$ and
    $\mathbb{U}$ is $h$-open in $\mathbb{X}$;

    \item \emph{regular-$h$-open} \cite{rodrigo2012international} if there exists a regular-open
    set $\mathbb{U}$ such that
    \[
    \mathbb{U}
    \subseteq\mathbb{A}
    \subseteq
    h\text{-}\operatorname{cl}(\mathbb{U});
    \]

    \item \emph{$rgh$-closed} \cite{rodrigo2012international} if
    \[
    h\text{-}\operatorname{cl}(\mathbb{A})
    \subseteq\mathbb{U},
    \]
    whenever $\mathbb{A}\subseteq\mathbb{U}$ and
    $\mathbb{U}$ is regular-$h$-open in $\mathbb{X}$;

    \item \emph{$hCg$-closed} \cite{rodrigo2012international} if
    \[
    h\text{-}\operatorname{cl}(\mathbb{A})
    \subseteq\mathbb{U},
    \]
    whenever $\mathbb{A}\subseteq\mathbb{U}$ and
    $\mathbb{U}$ is a $C$-set in $\mathbb{X}$.

\end{enumerate}
head: environment

label: def:Hstar-closed
title: Definition
body_md:
\label{def:Hstar-closed}
Let $\mathbb{A}\subseteq\mathbb{X}$. Then $\mathbb{A}$ is called
\emph{$H^{*}$-closed} \cite{Tomar2026} if
\[
h\text{-}\operatorname{cl}(\mathbb{A})
\subseteq\mathbb{U}
\]
whenever
\[
\mathbb{A}\subseteq\mathbb{U}
\]
and $\mathbb{U}$ is $hCg$-open in $\mathbb{X}$.

A subset $\mathbb{A}$ is called \emph{$H^{*}$-open} if
$\mathbb{X}\setminus\mathbb{A}$ is $H^{*}$-closed.
head: environment

label: prop:empty-X-Hstar
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{prop:empty-X-Hstar}
For every topological space $(\mathbb{X},\tau)$,
\[
\varnothing,\mathbb{X}\in H^{*}C(\mathbb{X})
\]
and consequently
\[
\varnothing,\mathbb{X}\in H^{*}O(\mathbb{X}).
\]
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Since
\[
h\text{-}\operatorname{cl}(\varnothing)=\varnothing,
\]
the defining condition of
Definition~\ref{def:Hstar-closed} is satisfied for
$\varnothing$. Hence
\[
\varnothing\in H^{*}C(\mathbb{X}).
\]

Now consider $\mathbb{X}$. If
\[
\mathbb{X}\subseteq\mathbb{U}\subseteq\mathbb{X},
\]
then necessarily $\mathbb{U}=\mathbb{X}$. Since
\[
h\text{-}\operatorname{cl}(\mathbb{X})=\mathbb{X},
\]
it follows that
\[
h\text{-}\operatorname{cl}(\mathbb{X})
\subseteq\mathbb{U}.
\]
Thus $\mathbb{X}$ is $H^{*}$-closed. The corresponding statements
for $H^{*}$-open sets follow immediately by taking complements.
head: environment

label: def:Hstar-operators
title: Definition
head: environment

label: prop:Hstar-basic-operators
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{prop:Hstar-basic-operators}
For all $\mathbb{A},\mathbb{B}\subseteq\mathbb{X}$, the following
statements hold:
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)]

    \item
    \[
    \mathbb{A}
    \subseteq
    H^{*}\operatorname{Cl}(\mathbb{A});
    \]

    \item if $\mathbb{A}\subseteq\mathbb{B}$, then
    \[
    H^{*}\operatorname{Cl}(\mathbb{A})
    \subseteq
    H^{*}\operatorname{Cl}(\mathbb{B});
    \]

    \item
    \[
    H^{*}\operatorname{Int}(\mathbb{A})
    \subseteq
    \mathbb{A};
    \]

    \item if $\mathbb{A}\subseteq\mathbb{B}$, then
    \[
    H^{*}\operatorname{Int}(\mathbb{A})
    \subseteq
    H^{*}\operatorname{Int}(\mathbb{B}).
    \]

\end{enumerate}
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Statement (i) follows directly from
\eqref{eq:Hstar-closure}, since every $H^{*}$-closed set occurring
in the defining intersection contains $\mathbb{A}$.

Suppose that $\mathbb{A}\subseteq\mathbb{B}$. Every
$H^{*}$-closed set containing $\mathbb{B}$ also contains
$\mathbb{A}$. Hence the family of $H^{*}$-closed supersets used to
define $H^{*}\operatorname{Cl}(\mathbb{B})$ is contained in the
corresponding family used to define
$H^{*}\operatorname{Cl}(\mathbb{A})$. Therefore,
\[
H^{*}\operatorname{Cl}(\mathbb{A})
\subseteq
H^{*}\operatorname{Cl}(\mathbb{B}),
\]
which proves (ii).

Statement (iii) follows from \eqref{eq:Hstar-interior}, since every
member of the defining union is contained in $\mathbb{A}$.

Finally, if $\mathbb{A}\subseteq\mathbb{B}$, every $H^{*}$-open
subset of $\mathbb{A}$ is also an $H^{*}$-open subset of
$\mathbb{B}$. Consequently,
\[
H^{*}\operatorname{Int}(\mathbb{A})
\subseteq
H^{*}\operatorname{Int}(\mathbb{B}),
\]
and (iv) follows.
head: environment

label: prop:Hstar-duality
title: Proposition
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
By Definition~\ref{def:Hstar-operators},
\[
H^{*}\operatorname{Int}(\mathbb{A})
=
\bigcup
\left\{
\mathbb{U}\in H^{*}O(\mathbb{X}):
\mathbb{U}\subseteq\mathbb{A}
\right\}.
\]
Since $\mathbb{U}$ is $H^{*}$-open if and only if
$\mathbb{X}\setminus\mathbb{U}$ is $H^{*}$-closed, the condition
$\mathbb{U}\subseteq\mathbb{A}$ is equivalent to
\[
\mathbb{X}\setminus\mathbb{A}
\subseteq
\mathbb{X}\setminus\mathbb{U}.
\]
Hence, by De Morgan's law,
\[
H^{*}\operatorname{Int}(\mathbb{A})
=
\mathbb{X}\setminus
\bigcap
\left\{
\mathbb{F}\in H^{*}C(\mathbb{X}):
\mathbb{X}\setminus\mathbb{A}\subseteq\mathbb{F}
\right\}.
\]
The intersection on the right-hand side is precisely
\[
H^{*}\operatorname{Cl}
(\mathbb{X}\setminus\mathbb{A}),
\]
which proves \eqref{eq:Hstar-int-cl-duality}. The second identity
follows by replacing $\mathbb{A}$ with
$\mathbb{X}\setminus\mathbb{A}$.
head: environment

label: def:generalized-topology
title: Definition
body_md:
\label{def:generalized-topology}
Let $\mathbb{X}$ be a nonempty set. A family
$\Gamma\subseteq\mathcal{P}(\mathbb{X})$ is called a
\emph{generalized topology} on $\mathbb{X}$ if:
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)]
    \item $\varnothing\in\Gamma$;
    \item for every family
    $\{\mathbb{U}_{\lambda}:\lambda\in\Lambda\}\subseteq\Gamma$,
    \[
    \bigcup_{\lambda\in\Lambda}\mathbb{U}_{\lambda}\in\Gamma.
    \]
\end{enumerate}
The pair $(\mathbb{X},\Gamma)$ is called a
\emph{generalized topological space}.
head: environment

label: def:strong-generalized-topology
title: Definition
body_md:
\label{def:strong-generalized-topology}
A generalized topology $\Gamma$ on $\mathbb{X}$ is called
\emph{strong} if
\[
\mathbb{X}\in\Gamma.
\]
In this case, $(\mathbb{X},\Gamma)$ is called a
\emph{strong generalized topological space}.
head: environment

label: def:Gamma-interior
title: Definition
body_md:
\label{def:Gamma-interior}
Let $(\mathbb{X},\Gamma)$ be a generalized topological space and
let $\mathbb{A}\subseteq\mathbb{X}$. The $\Gamma$-interior of
$\mathbb{A}$ is defined by
\[
i_{\Gamma}(\mathbb{A})
=
\bigcup
\left\{
\mathbb{U}\in\Gamma:
\mathbb{U}\subseteq\mathbb{A}
\right\}.
\]
head: environment

label: def:Gamma-closure
title: Definition
body_md:
\label{def:Gamma-closure}
Let $(\mathbb{X},\Gamma)$ be a generalized topological space. A
subset $\mathbb{F}\subseteq\mathbb{X}$ is called
$\Gamma$-closed if
\[
\mathbb{X}\setminus\mathbb{F}\in\Gamma.
\]
For $\mathbb{A}\subseteq\mathbb{X}$, the $\Gamma$-closure of
$\mathbb{A}$ is defined by
\[
c_{\Gamma}(\mathbb{A})
=
\bigcap
\left\{
\mathbb{F}\subseteq\mathbb{X}:
\mathbb{A}\subseteq\mathbb{F}
\text{ and }\mathbb{F}\text{ is }\Gamma\text{-closed}
\right\}.
\]
head: environment

label: rem:Hstar-not-automatic-topology
title: Remark
body_md:
\label{rem:Hstar-not-automatic-topology}
The family $H^{*}O(\mathbb{X})$ should not be identified with an
ordinary topology without additional assumptions.
Proposition~\ref{prop:empty-X-Hstar} guarantees only that
\[
\varnothing,\mathbb{X}\in H^{*}O(\mathbb{X}).
\]
Closure under arbitrary unions and closure under finite
intersections are separate structural requirements. In particular,
finite intersections of $H^{*}$-open sets need not, in general, be
$H^{*}$-open. Accordingly, the generalized-topological structure
and the associated ordinary topology, whenever the latter exists,
will be distinguished throughout the paper.
head: environment

label: thm:Hstar-strong-generalized-topology
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm:Hstar-strong-generalized-topology}
Let $(\mathbb{X},\tau)$ be a topological space. Suppose that
$H^{*}C(\mathbb{X})$ is closed under arbitrary intersections. Then
\[
\Gamma_{H^{*}}=H^{*}O(\mathbb{X})
\]
is a strong generalized topology on $\mathbb{X}$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
By Proposition~\ref{prop:empty-X-Hstar},
\[
\varnothing,\mathbb{X}\in H^{*}O(\mathbb{X}).
\]
It remains to verify closure under arbitrary unions.

Let
\[
\{\mathbb{U}_{\lambda}:\lambda\in\Lambda\}
\subseteq H^{*}O(\mathbb{X})
\]
be an arbitrary family. For every $\lambda\in\Lambda$,
\[
\mathbb{X}\setminus\mathbb{U}_{\lambda}
\in H^{*}C(\mathbb{X}).
\]
Since $H^{*}C(\mathbb{X})$ is closed under arbitrary intersections,
\[
\bigcap_{\lambda\in\Lambda}
\bigl(\mathbb{X}\setminus\mathbb{U}_{\lambda}\bigr)
\in H^{*}C(\mathbb{X}).
\]
By De Morgan's law,
\[
\mathbb{X}\setminus
\bigcup_{\lambda\in\Lambda}\mathbb{U}_{\lambda}
=
\bigcap_{\lambda\in\Lambda}
\bigl(\mathbb{X}\setminus\mathbb{U}_{\lambda}\bigr).
\]
Hence
\[
\mathbb{X}\setminus
\bigcup_{\lambda\in\Lambda}\mathbb{U}_{\lambda}
\in H^{*}C(\mathbb{X}),
\]
and therefore
\[
\bigcup_{\lambda\in\Lambda}\mathbb{U}_{\lambda}
\in H^{*}O(\mathbb{X}).
\]

Thus $H^{*}O(\mathbb{X})$ contains $\varnothing$ and
$\mathbb{X}$ and is closed under arbitrary unions. Consequently,
\[
\Gamma_{H^{*}}=H^{*}O(\mathbb{X})
\]
is a strong generalized topology on $\mathbb{X}$.
head: environment

label: prop:Gamma-Hstar-closed
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{prop:Gamma-Hstar-closed}
Under the hypothesis of
Theorem~\ref{thm:Hstar-strong-generalized-topology}, a subset
$\mathbb{F}\subseteq\mathbb{X}$ is
$\Gamma_{H^{*}}$-closed if and only if it is $H^{*}$-closed.
Consequently,
\[
\mathcal{C}_{\Gamma_{H^{*}}}
=
H^{*}C(\mathbb{X}),
\]
where $\mathcal{C}_{\Gamma_{H^{*}}}$ denotes the family of all
$\Gamma_{H^{*}}$-closed subsets of $\mathbb{X}$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
By definition, $\mathbb{F}$ is $\Gamma_{H^{*}}$-closed if and only if
\[
\mathbb{X}\setminus\mathbb{F}\in\Gamma_{H^{*}}.
\]
Since
\[
\Gamma_{H^{*}}=H^{*}O(\mathbb{X}),
\]
this is equivalent to
\[
\mathbb{X}\setminus\mathbb{F}\in H^{*}O(\mathbb{X}).
\]
By the definition of an $H^{*}$-open set, the latter holds if and
only if
\[
\mathbb{F}\in H^{*}C(\mathbb{X}).
\]
Hence the two families of closed sets coincide.
head: environment

label: thm:Gamma-Hstar-operators
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm:Gamma-Hstar-operators}
Let $(\mathbb{X},\tau)$ satisfy the hypothesis of
Theorem~\ref{thm:Hstar-strong-generalized-topology}. Then, for every
$\mathbb{A}\subseteq\mathbb{X}$,
\[
c_{\Gamma_{H^{*}}}(\mathbb{A})
=
H^{*}\operatorname{Cl}(\mathbb{A})
\]
and
\[
i_{\Gamma_{H^{*}}}(\mathbb{A})
=
H^{*}\operatorname{Int}(\mathbb{A}).
\]
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
By Definition~\ref{def:Gamma-closure},
\[
c_{\Gamma_{H^{*}}}(\mathbb{A})
=
\bigcap
\left\{
\mathbb{F}\subseteq\mathbb{X}:
\mathbb{A}\subseteq\mathbb{F}
\text{ and }
\mathbb{F}\text{ is }\Gamma_{H^{*}}\text{-closed}
\right\}.
\]
By Proposition~\ref{prop:Gamma-Hstar-closed}, the
$\Gamma_{H^{*}}$-closed sets are precisely the $H^{*}$-closed sets.
Therefore,
\[
c_{\Gamma_{H^{*}}}(\mathbb{A})
=
\bigcap
\left\{
\mathbb{F}\in H^{*}C(\mathbb{X}):
\mathbb{A}\subseteq\mathbb{F}
\right\}
=
H^{*}\operatorname{Cl}(\mathbb{A}).
\]

Similarly,
\[
i_{\Gamma_{H^{*}}}(\mathbb{A})
=
\bigcup
\left\{
\mathbb{U}\in\Gamma_{H^{*}}:
\mathbb{U}\subseteq\mathbb{A}
\right\}.
\]
Since $\Gamma_{H^{*}}=H^{*}O(\mathbb{X})$, we obtain
\[
i_{\Gamma_{H^{*}}}(\mathbb{A})
=
\bigcup
\left\{
\mathbb{U}\in H^{*}O(\mathbb{X}):
\mathbb{U}\subseteq\mathbb{A}
\right\}
=
H^{*}\operatorname{Int}(\mathbb{A}).
\]
head: environment

label: cor:Hstar-closure-closed
title: Corollary
body_md:
\label{cor:Hstar-closure-closed}
Under the hypothesis of
Theorem~\ref{thm:Hstar-strong-generalized-topology}, for every
$\mathbb{A}\subseteq\mathbb{X}$,
\[
H^{*}\operatorname{Cl}(\mathbb{A})
\in H^{*}C(\mathbb{X})
\]
and
\[
H^{*}\operatorname{Int}(\mathbb{A})
\in H^{*}O(\mathbb{X}).
\]
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Since $H^{*}C(\mathbb{X})$ is closed under arbitrary intersections,
the intersection defining
$H^{*}\operatorname{Cl}(\mathbb{A})$ is $H^{*}$-closed.

Moreover, by
Theorem~\ref{thm:Hstar-strong-generalized-topology},
$H^{*}O(\mathbb{X})$ is closed under arbitrary unions. Hence the
union defining $H^{*}\operatorname{Int}(\mathbb{A})$ is
$H^{*}$-open.
head: environment

label: cor:Hstar-fixed-points
title: Corollary
body_md:
\label{cor:Hstar-fixed-points}
Under the hypothesis of
Theorem~\ref{thm:Hstar-strong-generalized-topology}, for every
$\mathbb{A}\subseteq\mathbb{X}$:
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)]
    \item $\mathbb{A}$ is $H^{*}$-closed if and only if
    \[
    H^{*}\operatorname{Cl}(\mathbb{A})=\mathbb{A};
    \]

    \item $\mathbb{A}$ is $H^{*}$-open if and only if
    \[
    H^{*}\operatorname{Int}(\mathbb{A})=\mathbb{A}.
    \]
\end{enumerate}
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Suppose first that $\mathbb{A}$ is $H^{*}$-closed. Since
$\mathbb{A}$ itself occurs among the $H^{*}$-closed supersets in the
definition of $H^{*}\operatorname{Cl}(\mathbb{A})$,
\[
H^{*}\operatorname{Cl}(\mathbb{A})\subseteq\mathbb{A}.
\]
By Proposition~\ref{prop:Hstar-basic-operators},
\[
\mathbb{A}\subseteq
H^{*}\operatorname{Cl}(\mathbb{A}),
\]
and therefore
\[
H^{*}\operatorname{Cl}(\mathbb{A})=\mathbb{A}.
\]

Conversely, if
\[
H^{*}\operatorname{Cl}(\mathbb{A})=\mathbb{A},
\]
then Corollary~\ref{cor:Hstar-closure-closed} implies that
$\mathbb{A}$ is $H^{*}$-closed.

The proof of (ii) is dual.
head: environment

label: thm:Hstar-topology-characterization
title: Theorem
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
By Theorem~\ref{thm:Hstar-strong-generalized-topology},
$\Gamma_{H^{*}}=H^{*}O(\mathbb{X})$ contains
$\varnothing$ and $\mathbb{X}$ and is closed under arbitrary unions.
Therefore, it is an ordinary topology precisely when it is also
closed under finite intersections. Thus (i) and (ii) are equivalent.

Assume (ii), and let
$\mathbb{F}_{1},\mathbb{F}_{2}\in H^{*}C(\mathbb{X})$. Then
\[
\mathbb{X}\setminus\mathbb{F}_{1},
\quad
\mathbb{X}\setminus\mathbb{F}_{2}
\in H^{*}O(\mathbb{X}).
\]
By (ii),
\[
(\mathbb{X}\setminus\mathbb{F}_{1})
\cap
(\mathbb{X}\setminus\mathbb{F}_{2})
\in H^{*}O(\mathbb{X}).
\]
Since
\[
(\mathbb{X}\setminus\mathbb{F}_{1})
\cap
(\mathbb{X}\setminus\mathbb{F}_{2})
=
\mathbb{X}\setminus
(\mathbb{F}_{1}\cup\mathbb{F}_{2}),
\]
we obtain
\[
\mathbb{F}_{1}\cup\mathbb{F}_{2}
\in H^{*}C(\mathbb{X}).
\]
Hence (iii) holds.

Conversely, assume (iii), and let
$\mathbb{U}_{1},\mathbb{U}_{2}\in H^{*}O(\mathbb{X})$. Then
\[
\mathbb{X}\setminus\mathbb{U}_{1},
\quad
\mathbb{X}\setminus\mathbb{U}_{2}
\in H^{*}C(\mathbb{X}).
\]
By (iii),
\[
(\mathbb{X}\setminus\mathbb{U}_{1})
\cup
(\mathbb{X}\setminus\mathbb{U}_{2})
\in H^{*}C(\mathbb{X}).
\]
Using De Morgan's law,
\[
(\mathbb{X}\setminus\mathbb{U}_{1})
\cup
(\mathbb{X}\setminus\mathbb{U}_{2})
=
\mathbb{X}\setminus
(\mathbb{U}_{1}\cap\mathbb{U}_{2}).
\]
Therefore,
\[
\mathbb{U}_{1}\cap\mathbb{U}_{2}
\in H^{*}O(\mathbb{X}),
\]
and (ii) follows.
head: environment

label: def:associated-Hstar-topology
title: Definition
body_md:
\label{def:associated-Hstar-topology}
Whenever the equivalent conditions of
Theorem~\ref{thm:Hstar-topology-characterization} are satisfied, we
write
\[
\tau_{H^{*}}=H^{*}O(\mathbb{X})
\]
and call $\tau_{H^{*}}$ the \emph{topology induced by the
$H^{*}$-open sets}. The space
\[
(\mathbb{X},\tau_{H^{*}})
\]
will be referred to as the \emph{associated $H^{*}$-topological
space}.
head: environment

label: rem:Gamma-vs-tau
title: Remark
body_md:
\label{rem:Gamma-vs-tau}
The symbols $\Gamma_{H^{*}}$ and $\tau_{H^{*}}$ have distinct
meanings. The notation
\[
\Gamma_{H^{*}}=H^{*}O(\mathbb{X})
\]
is used when the hypotheses establishing a strong generalized
topology are satisfied, whereas
\[
\tau_{H^{*}}=H^{*}O(\mathbb{X})
\]
is used only when the additional finite-intersection condition of
Theorem~\ref{thm:Hstar-topology-characterization} is satisfied.
Thus, the existence of $\Gamma_{H^{*}}$ does not by itself imply the
existence of the associated ordinary topology $\tau_{H^{*}}$.
head: environment

label: ex:Hstar-not-topology
title: Example
body_md:
\label{ex:Hstar-not-topology}
Let
\[
\mathbb{X}=\{k,l,m,n\}
\]
and consider the topology
\[
\tau=
\{
\varnothing,\mathbb{X},
\{k\},\{l\},\{k,l\},\{k,m\},\{k,l,m\}
\}.
\]
For this space, the family of $H^{*}$-closed sets is
\[
\begin{aligned}
H^{*}C(\mathbb{X})
=
\{&
\varnothing,\mathbb{X},
\{k\},\{l\},\{m\},\{n\},
\{k,m\},\{k,n\},\\
&
\{l,m\},\{l,n\},\{m,n\},
\{k,l,n\},\{k,m,n\},\{l,m,n\}
\}.
\end{aligned}
\]

In particular,
\[
\{k\},\{l\}\in H^{*}C(\mathbb{X}),
\]
whereas
\[
\{k,l\}\notin H^{*}C(\mathbb{X}).
\]
Thus $H^{*}C(\mathbb{X})$ is not closed under finite unions.

Equivalently,
\[
\mathbb{X}\setminus\{k\}=\{l,m,n\}
\]
and
\[
\mathbb{X}\setminus\{l\}=\{k,m,n\}
\]
belong to $H^{*}O(\mathbb{X})$. However,
\[
\{l,m,n\}\cap\{k,m,n\}
=
\{m,n\},
\]
while
\[
\mathbb{X}\setminus\{m,n\}=\{k,l\}
\notin H^{*}C(\mathbb{X}).
\]
Therefore,
\[
\{m,n\}\notin H^{*}O(\mathbb{X}).
\]

Hence $H^{*}O(\mathbb{X})$ is not closed under finite intersections
and therefore does not form an ordinary topology on $\mathbb{X}$.
head: environment

label: rem:need-generalized-topology
title: Remark
body_md:
\label{rem:need-generalized-topology}
Example~\ref{ex:Hstar-not-topology} shows that the family of
$H^{*}$-open sets cannot, in general, be treated as an ordinary
topology. Therefore, the generalized-topological structure
$\Gamma_{H^{*}}$ is considered only under the hypothesis of
Theorem~\ref{thm:Hstar-strong-generalized-topology}, while the
ordinary topology $\tau_{H^{*}}$ is introduced only when the
additional equivalent conditions of
Theorem~\ref{thm:Hstar-topology-characterization} are satisfied.
head: environment

label: thm:Hstar-closure-properties
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm:Hstar-closure-properties}
For all $\mathbb{A},\mathbb{B}\subseteq\mathbb{X}$, the
$H^{*}$-closure operator satisfies:
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)]

    \item
    \[
    H^{*}\operatorname{Cl}(\varnothing)=\varnothing;
    \]

    \item
    \[
    H^{*}\operatorname{Cl}(\mathbb{X})=\mathbb{X};
    \]

    \item
    \[
    \mathbb{A}
    \subseteq
    H^{*}\operatorname{Cl}(\mathbb{A});
    \]

    \item if $\mathbb{A}\subseteq\mathbb{B}$, then
    \[
    H^{*}\operatorname{Cl}(\mathbb{A})
    \subseteq
    H^{*}\operatorname{Cl}(\mathbb{B});
    \]

    \item
    \[
    H^{*}\operatorname{Cl}
    \bigl(H^{*}\operatorname{Cl}(\mathbb{A})\bigr)
    =
    H^{*}\operatorname{Cl}(\mathbb{A}).
    \]

\end{enumerate}
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Since $\varnothing$ is $H^{*}$-closed,
\[
H^{*}\operatorname{Cl}(\varnothing)
\subseteq\varnothing,
\]
and hence
\[
H^{*}\operatorname{Cl}(\varnothing)=\varnothing.
\]

Since $\mathbb{X}$ is $H^{*}$-closed and is the only subset of
$\mathbb{X}$ containing $\mathbb{X}$, we obtain
\[
H^{*}\operatorname{Cl}(\mathbb{X})=\mathbb{X}.
\]

The extensivity and monotonicity assertions in (iii) and (iv)
follow from Proposition~\ref{prop:Hstar-basic-operators}.

Finally, by
Corollary~\ref{cor:Hstar-closure-closed},
$H^{*}\operatorname{Cl}(\mathbb{A})$ is itself $H^{*}$-closed.
Applying
Corollary~\ref{cor:Hstar-fixed-points} therefore gives
\[
H^{*}\operatorname{Cl}
\bigl(H^{*}\operatorname{Cl}(\mathbb{A})\bigr)
=
H^{*}\operatorname{Cl}(\mathbb{A}).
\]
head: environment

label: thm:Hstar-interior-properties
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm:Hstar-interior-properties}
For all $\mathbb{A},\mathbb{B}\subseteq\mathbb{X}$, the
$H^{*}$-interior operator satisfies:
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)]

    \item
    \[
    H^{*}\operatorname{Int}(\varnothing)=\varnothing;
    \]

    \item
    \[
    H^{*}\operatorname{Int}(\mathbb{X})=\mathbb{X};
    \]

    \item
    \[
    H^{*}\operatorname{Int}(\mathbb{A})
    \subseteq\mathbb{A};
    \]

    \item if $\mathbb{A}\subseteq\mathbb{B}$, then
    \[
    H^{*}\operatorname{Int}(\mathbb{A})
    \subseteq
    H^{*}\operatorname{Int}(\mathbb{B});
    \]

    \item
    \[
    H^{*}\operatorname{Int}
    \bigl(H^{*}\operatorname{Int}(\mathbb{A})\bigr)
    =
    H^{*}\operatorname{Int}(\mathbb{A}).
    \]

\end{enumerate}
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Since
\[
\varnothing,\mathbb{X}\in H^{*}O(\mathbb{X}),
\]
the first two assertions follow directly from the definition of
$H^{*}$-interior.

Assertions (iii) and (iv) follow from
Proposition~\ref{prop:Hstar-basic-operators}.

By Theorem~\ref{thm:Hstar-strong-generalized-topology},
$H^{*}O(\mathbb{X})$ is closed under arbitrary unions. Hence
$H^{*}\operatorname{Int}(\mathbb{A})$ is itself $H^{*}$-open.
Corollary~\ref{cor:Hstar-fixed-points} therefore yields
\[
H^{*}\operatorname{Int}
\bigl(H^{*}\operatorname{Int}(\mathbb{A})\bigr)
=
H^{*}\operatorname{Int}(\mathbb{A}).
\]
head: environment

label: prop:Hstar-union-intersection
title: Proposition
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Since
\[
\mathbb{A}\subseteq\mathbb{A}\cup\mathbb{B}
\quad\text{and}\quad
\mathbb{B}\subseteq\mathbb{A}\cup\mathbb{B},
\]
monotonicity of $H^{*}\operatorname{Cl}$ gives
\[
H^{*}\operatorname{Cl}(\mathbb{A})
\subseteq
H^{*}\operatorname{Cl}(\mathbb{A}\cup\mathbb{B})
\]
and
\[
H^{*}\operatorname{Cl}(\mathbb{B})
\subseteq
H^{*}\operatorname{Cl}(\mathbb{A}\cup\mathbb{B}).
\]
Taking the union of these inclusions yields
\eqref{eq:Hstar-closure-union-inclusion}.

Similarly,
\[
\mathbb{A}\cap\mathbb{B}\subseteq\mathbb{A}
\quad\text{and}\quad
\mathbb{A}\cap\mathbb{B}\subseteq\mathbb{B}.
\]
Monotonicity of $H^{*}\operatorname{Int}$ therefore gives
\[
H^{*}\operatorname{Int}(\mathbb{A}\cap\mathbb{B})
\subseteq
H^{*}\operatorname{Int}(\mathbb{A})
\]
and
\[
H^{*}\operatorname{Int}(\mathbb{A}\cap\mathbb{B})
\subseteq
H^{*}\operatorname{Int}(\mathbb{B}).
\]
Hence
\[
H^{*}\operatorname{Int}(\mathbb{A}\cap\mathbb{B})
\subseteq
H^{*}\operatorname{Int}(\mathbb{A})
\cap
H^{*}\operatorname{Int}(\mathbb{B}).
\]
head: environment

label: rem:Hstar-no-equality-general
title: Remark
body_md:
\label{rem:Hstar-no-equality-general}
At the level of a strong generalized topology, the inclusions in
Proposition~\ref{prop:Hstar-union-intersection} need not become
equalities. The reverse inclusions require additional finite
intersection or, equivalently, finite union structure. Thus these
equalities arise naturally when the associated ordinary topology
$\tau_{H^{*}}$ exists.
head: environment

label: thm:Hstar-Kuratowski
title: Theorem
head: environment
name: Finite Union and Intersection Laws

title: Proof
body_md:
Under the stated hypothesis,
\[
\tau_{H^{*}}=H^{*}O(\mathbb{X})
\]
is an ordinary topology. By
Theorem~\ref{thm:Hstar-topology-characterization},
$H^{*}C(\mathbb{X})$ is therefore closed under finite unions.

Since
$H^{*}\operatorname{Cl}(\mathbb{A})$ and
$H^{*}\operatorname{Cl}(\mathbb{B})$ are $H^{*}$-closed, their
union is $H^{*}$-closed and contains
$\mathbb{A}\cup\mathbb{B}$. By the definition of
$H^{*}$-closure,
\[
H^{*}\operatorname{Cl}(\mathbb{A}\cup\mathbb{B})
\subseteq
H^{*}\operatorname{Cl}(\mathbb{A})
\cup
H^{*}\operatorname{Cl}(\mathbb{B}).
\]
The reverse inclusion follows from
Proposition~\ref{prop:Hstar-union-intersection}. Hence
\[
H^{*}\operatorname{Cl}(\mathbb{A}\cup\mathbb{B})
=
H^{*}\operatorname{Cl}(\mathbb{A})
\cup
H^{*}\operatorname{Cl}(\mathbb{B}).
\]

The corresponding interior identity follows either by the dual
argument or from
\eqref{eq:Hstar-closure-duality} and De Morgan's law.
head: environment

label: cor:Hstar-associated-closure
title: Corollary
body_md:
\label{cor:Hstar-associated-closure}
If
\[
\tau_{H^{*}}=H^{*}O(\mathbb{X})
\]
is an ordinary topology, then, for every
$\mathbb{A}\subseteq\mathbb{X}$,
\[
H^{*}\operatorname{Cl}(\mathbb{A})
=
\operatorname{Cl}_{\tau_{H^{*}}}(\mathbb{A})
\]
and
\[
H^{*}\operatorname{Int}(\mathbb{A})
=
\operatorname{Int}_{\tau_{H^{*}}}(\mathbb{A}).
\]
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
The closed sets of $(\mathbb{X},\tau_{H^{*}})$ are precisely the
complements of members of
\[
\tau_{H^{*}}=H^{*}O(\mathbb{X}),
\]
and therefore they are exactly the members of
$H^{*}C(\mathbb{X})$. Hence the ordinary
$\tau_{H^{*}}$-closure and the $H^{*}$-closure are obtained from
the same family of closed supersets. Consequently,
\[
H^{*}\operatorname{Cl}(\mathbb{A})
=
\operatorname{Cl}_{\tau_{H^{*}}}(\mathbb{A}).
\]

Similarly, the open sets of $\tau_{H^{*}}$ are exactly the members
of $H^{*}O(\mathbb{X})$. Thus
\[
H^{*}\operatorname{Int}(\mathbb{A})
=
\operatorname{Int}_{\tau_{H^{*}}}(\mathbb{A}).
\]
head: environment

label: def:Hstar-separation
title: Definition
body_md:
\label{def:Hstar-separation}
Let $(\mathbb{X},\tau)$ be a topological space.
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)]

    \item The space $(\mathbb{X},\tau)$ is said to be
    \emph{$H^{*}$-$T_{0}$} if, for every pair of distinct points
    $k,l\in\mathbb{X}$, there exists an $H^{*}$-open set containing
    one of them but not the other.

    \item The space $(\mathbb{X},\tau)$ is said to be
    \emph{$H^{*}$-$T_{1}$} if, for every pair of distinct points
    $k,l\in\mathbb{X}$, there exist $H^{*}$-open sets
    $\mathbb{U}$ and $\mathbb{V}$ such that
    \[
    k\in\mathbb{U},\qquad l\notin\mathbb{U},
    \]
    and
    \[
    l\in\mathbb{V},\qquad k\notin\mathbb{V}.
    \]

    \item The space $(\mathbb{X},\tau)$ is said to be
    \emph{$H^{*}$-$T_{2}$} if, for every pair of distinct points
    $k,l\in\mathbb{X}$, there exist disjoint $H^{*}$-open sets
    $\mathbb{U}$ and $\mathbb{V}$ such that
    \[
    k\in\mathbb{U},
    \qquad
    l\in\mathbb{V}.
    \]

\end{enumerate}
head: environment

label: prop:Hstar-separation-chain
title: Proposition
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Suppose that $(\mathbb{X},\tau)$ is $H^{*}$-$T_{2}$ and let
$k,l\in\mathbb{X}$ with $k\neq l$. Then there exist disjoint
$H^{*}$-open sets $\mathbb{U}$ and $\mathbb{V}$ such that
\[
k\in\mathbb{U}
\qquad\text{and}\qquad
l\in\mathbb{V}.
\]
Since
\[
\mathbb{U}\cap\mathbb{V}=\varnothing,
\]
we have
\[
l\notin\mathbb{U}
\qquad\text{and}\qquad
k\notin\mathbb{V}.
\]
Hence $(\mathbb{X},\tau)$ is $H^{*}$-$T_{1}$.

The implication
\[
H^{*}\text{-}T_{1}
\Longrightarrow
H^{*}\text{-}T_{0}
\]
follows immediately from Definition~\ref{def:Hstar-separation}.
head: environment

label: thm:Hstar-T1-singletons
title: Theorem
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Suppose first that $(\mathbb{X},\tau)$ is $H^{*}$-$T_{1}$.
Fix $k\in\mathbb{X}$. For every
$l\in\mathbb{X}\setminus\{k\}$, there exists an $H^{*}$-open set
$\mathbb{U}_{l}$ such that
\[
l\in\mathbb{U}_{l}
\qquad\text{and}\qquad
k\notin\mathbb{U}_{l}.
\]
Therefore,
\[
\mathbb{X}\setminus\{k\}
=
\bigcup_{l\in\mathbb{X}\setminus\{k\}}
\mathbb{U}_{l}.
\]
Since $H^{*}O(\mathbb{X})$ is closed under arbitrary unions,
$\mathbb{X}\setminus\{k\}$ is $H^{*}$-open. Hence
$\{k\}$ is $H^{*}$-closed.

Conversely, suppose that every singleton subset of $\mathbb{X}$ is
$H^{*}$-closed. Let $k,l\in\mathbb{X}$ with $k\neq l$. Then
\[
\mathbb{X}\setminus\{l\}
\quad\text{and}\quad
\mathbb{X}\setminus\{k\}
\]
are $H^{*}$-open. Moreover,
\[
k\in\mathbb{X}\setminus\{l\},
\qquad
l\notin\mathbb{X}\setminus\{l\},
\]
and
\[
l\in\mathbb{X}\setminus\{k\},
\qquad
k\notin\mathbb{X}\setminus\{k\}.
\]
Thus $(\mathbb{X},\tau)$ is $H^{*}$-$T_{1}$.
head: environment

label: def:Hstar-D-set
title: Definition
body_md:
\label{def:Hstar-D-set}
A subset $\mathbb{D}\subseteq\mathbb{X}$ is called an
\emph{$H^{*}$-difference set}, briefly an \emph{$H^{*}D$-set}, if
there exist
\[
\mathbb{U},\mathbb{V}\in H^{*}O(\mathbb{X})
\]
such that
\[
\mathbb{D}=\mathbb{U}\setminus\mathbb{V}
\]
and
\[
\mathbb{U}\neq\mathbb{X}.
\]
head: environment

label: def:Hstar-D1-D2
title: Definition
body_md:
\label{def:Hstar-D1-D2}
The space $(\mathbb{X},\tau)$ is said to be:
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)]

    \item \emph{$H^{*}$-$D_{1}$} if, for every pair of distinct
    points $k,l\in\mathbb{X}$, there exist $H^{*}D$-sets
    $\mathbb{D}_{1}$ and $\mathbb{D}_{2}$ such that
    \[
    k\in\mathbb{D}_{1},\qquad
    l\notin\mathbb{D}_{1},
    \]
    and
    \[
    l\in\mathbb{D}_{2},\qquad
    k\notin\mathbb{D}_{2};
    \]

    \item \emph{$H^{*}$-$D_{2}$} if, for every pair of distinct
    points $k,l\in\mathbb{X}$, there exist disjoint $H^{*}D$-sets
    $\mathbb{D}_{1}$ and $\mathbb{D}_{2}$ such that
    \[
    k\in\mathbb{D}_{1},
    \qquad
    l\in\mathbb{D}_{2}.
    \]

\end{enumerate}
head: environment

label: prop:Hstar-D2-D1
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{prop:Hstar-D2-D1}
Every $H^{*}$-$D_{2}$ space is an $H^{*}$-$D_{1}$ space.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Let $k,l\in\mathbb{X}$ be distinct. Since the space is
$H^{*}$-$D_{2}$, there exist disjoint $H^{*}D$-sets
$\mathbb{D}_{1}$ and $\mathbb{D}_{2}$ such that
\[
k\in\mathbb{D}_{1}
\qquad\text{and}\qquad
l\in\mathbb{D}_{2}.
\]
Their disjointness implies
\[
l\notin\mathbb{D}_{1}
\qquad\text{and}\qquad
k\notin\mathbb{D}_{2}.
\]
Hence the defining conditions of an $H^{*}$-$D_{1}$ space are
satisfied.
head: environment

label: prop:Hstar-D1-T0
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{prop:Hstar-D1-T0}
Every $H^{*}$-$D_{1}$ space is an $H^{*}$-$T_{0}$ space.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Let $k,l\in\mathbb{X}$ with $k\neq l$. Since
$(\mathbb{X},\tau)$ is $H^{*}$-$D_{1}$, there exists an
$H^{*}D$-set $\mathbb{D}$ such that
\[
k\in\mathbb{D}
\qquad\text{and}\qquad
l\notin\mathbb{D}.
\]
Write
\[
\mathbb{D}=\mathbb{U}\setminus\mathbb{V},
\]
where
\[
\mathbb{U},\mathbb{V}\in H^{*}O(\mathbb{X})
\qquad\text{and}\qquad
\mathbb{U}\neq\mathbb{X}.
\]
Since $k\in\mathbb{D}$,
\[
k\in\mathbb{U}
\qquad\text{and}\qquad
k\notin\mathbb{V}.
\]

If $l\notin\mathbb{U}$, then $\mathbb{U}$ is an $H^{*}$-open set
containing $k$ but not $l$.

If $l\in\mathbb{U}$, then $l\notin\mathbb{D}$ implies
$l\in\mathbb{V}$. Hence $\mathbb{V}$ is an $H^{*}$-open set
containing $l$ but not $k$.

Thus one of the two points belongs to an $H^{*}$-open set that does
not contain the other. Therefore $(\mathbb{X},\tau)$ is
$H^{*}$-$T_{0}$.
head: environment

label: thm:Hstar-T0-associated
title: Theorem
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
The assertion follows immediately from
\[
\tau_{H^{*}}=H^{*}O(\mathbb{X}),
\]
since both conditions require exactly the same open-set separation
of every pair of distinct points.
head: environment

label: thm:Hstar-T1-associated
title: Theorem
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Since
\[
\tau_{H^{*}}=H^{*}O(\mathbb{X}),
\]
the $H^{*}$-open sets occurring in
Definition~\ref{def:Hstar-separation} are precisely the open sets of
$\tau_{H^{*}}$. Hence the two $T_{1}$ conditions are identical.
head: environment

label: thm:Hstar-T2-associated
title: Theorem
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Again,
\[
\tau_{H^{*}}=H^{*}O(\mathbb{X}).
\]
Thus disjoint $H^{*}$-open neighbourhoods of two distinct points are
exactly disjoint $\tau_{H^{*}}$-open neighbourhoods of those points.
The equivalence follows.
head: environment

label: cor:Hstar-Ti-associated
title: Corollary
body_md:
\label{cor:Hstar-Ti-associated}
For $i\in\{0,1,2\}$,
\[
(\mathbb{X},\tau)
\text{ is }H^{*}\text{-}T_{i}
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
(\mathbb{X},\tau_{H^{*}})
\text{ is }T_{i}.
\]
head: environment

label: def:classical-D-set
title: Definition
body_md:
\label{def:classical-D-set}
Let $(\mathbb{X},\sigma)$ be a topological space. A subset
$\mathbb{D}\subseteq\mathbb{X}$ is called a \emph{$D$-set} if
\[
\mathbb{D}=\mathbb{U}\setminus\mathbb{V},
\]
where
\[
\mathbb{U},\mathbb{V}\in\sigma
\qquad\text{and}\qquad
\mathbb{U}\neq\mathbb{X}.
\]
head: environment

label: prop:Hstar-D-classical-D
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{prop:Hstar-D-classical-D}
A subset $\mathbb{D}\subseteq\mathbb{X}$ is an $H^{*}D$-set in
$(\mathbb{X},\tau)$ if and only if it is a $D$-set in
$(\mathbb{X},\tau_{H^{*}})$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
By Definition~\ref{def:Hstar-D-set}, $\mathbb{D}$ is an
$H^{*}D$-set if and only if
\[
\mathbb{D}=\mathbb{U}\setminus\mathbb{V},
\]
where
\[
\mathbb{U},\mathbb{V}\in H^{*}O(\mathbb{X})
\qquad\text{and}\qquad
\mathbb{U}\neq\mathbb{X}.
\]
Since
\[
H^{*}O(\mathbb{X})=\tau_{H^{*}},
\]
this is precisely the definition of a $D$-set in
$(\mathbb{X},\tau_{H^{*}})$.
head: environment

label: thm:Hstar-D-associated
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm:Hstar-D-associated}
For $i\in\{1,2\}$,
\[
(\mathbb{X},\tau)
\text{ is }H^{*}\text{-}D_{i}
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
(\mathbb{X},\tau_{H^{*}})
\text{ is }D_{i}.
\]
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
By Proposition~\ref{prop:Hstar-D-classical-D}, the $H^{*}D$-sets of
$(\mathbb{X},\tau)$ are exactly the $D$-sets of
$(\mathbb{X},\tau_{H^{*}})$. Hence the point-separation conditions
defining $H^{*}$-$D_{1}$ and $H^{*}$-$D_{2}$ coincide,
respectively, with the classical $D_{1}$ and $D_{2}$ conditions in
the associated topology.
head: environment

label: cor:Hstar-D1-D2-associated
title: Corollary
body_md:
\label{cor:Hstar-D1-D2-associated}
If the classical $D_{1}$ and $D_{2}$ conditions are equivalent in
$(\mathbb{X},\tau_{H^{*}})$, then
\[
(\mathbb{X},\tau)
\text{ is }H^{*}\text{-}D_{1}
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
(\mathbb{X},\tau)
\text{ is }H^{*}\text{-}D_{2}.
\]
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
This follows immediately from
Theorem~\ref{thm:Hstar-D-associated}.
head: environment

label: rem:associated-separation-interpretation
title: Remark
body_md:
\label{rem:associated-separation-interpretation}
Whenever the associated topology exists, the preceding equivalences
should be viewed as structural identifications rather than as
independent separation phenomena. Indeed, the open sets of
$(\mathbb{X},\tau_{H^{*}})$ are exactly the $H^{*}$-open sets of
$(\mathbb{X},\tau)$. Consequently, the $H^{*}$-$T_i$ conditions
and the corresponding $H^{*}$-difference separation conditions
translate directly into their classical counterparts in the
associated topology. This provides the bridge needed for the
higher separation properties considered in the next section.
head: environment

label: def:Hstar-regular
title: Definition
body_md:
\label{def:Hstar-regular}
A topological space $(\mathbb{X},\tau)$ is said to be
\emph{$H^{*}$-regular} if, whenever
$\mathbb{F}\in H^{*}C(\mathbb{X})$ and
$k\in\mathbb{X}\setminus\mathbb{F}$, there exist disjoint
$H^{*}$-open sets $\mathbb{U}$ and $\mathbb{V}$ such that
\[
k\in\mathbb{U}
\qquad\text{and}\qquad
\mathbb{F}\subseteq\mathbb{V}.
\]
head: environment

label: thm:Hstar-regular-associated
title: Theorem
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Suppose that $(\mathbb{X},\tau)$ is $H^{*}$-regular. Let
$\mathbb{F}$ be a closed subset of
$(\mathbb{X},\tau_{H^{*}})$ and let
\[
k\in\mathbb{X}\setminus\mathbb{F}.
\]
Since the $\tau_{H^{*}}$-closed sets are precisely the
$H^{*}$-closed sets,
\[
\mathbb{F}\in H^{*}C(\mathbb{X}).
\]
By $H^{*}$-regularity, there exist disjoint $H^{*}$-open sets
$\mathbb{U}$ and $\mathbb{V}$ such that
\[
k\in\mathbb{U},
\qquad
\mathbb{F}\subseteq\mathbb{V}.
\]
Since
\[
H^{*}O(\mathbb{X})=\tau_{H^{*}},
\]
the sets $\mathbb{U}$ and $\mathbb{V}$ are
$\tau_{H^{*}}$-open. Hence $(\mathbb{X},\tau_{H^{*}})$ is regular.

Conversely, suppose that $(\mathbb{X},\tau_{H^{*}})$ is regular.
Let $\mathbb{F}\in H^{*}C(\mathbb{X})$ and let
\[
k\in\mathbb{X}\setminus\mathbb{F}.
\]
Then $\mathbb{F}$ is $\tau_{H^{*}}$-closed. By regularity, there
exist disjoint $\tau_{H^{*}}$-open sets $\mathbb{U}$ and
$\mathbb{V}$ such that
\[
k\in\mathbb{U},
\qquad
\mathbb{F}\subseteq\mathbb{V}.
\]
Since the $\tau_{H^{*}}$-open sets are exactly the $H^{*}$-open
sets, $(\mathbb{X},\tau)$ is $H^{*}$-regular.
head: environment

label: def:Hstar-T3
title: Definition
body_md:
\label{def:Hstar-T3}
The space $(\mathbb{X},\tau)$ is called an
\emph{$H^{*}$-$T_{3}$ space} if it is both $H^{*}$-regular and
$H^{*}$-$T_{1}$.
head: environment

label: cor:Hstar-T3-associated
title: Corollary
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
This follows from
Theorem~\ref{thm:Hstar-regular-associated} together with
Theorem~\ref{thm:Hstar-T1-associated}.
head: environment

label: def:Hstar-normal
title: Definition
body_md:
\label{def:Hstar-normal}
A topological space $(\mathbb{X},\tau)$ is said to be
\emph{$H^{*}$-normal} if, for every pair of disjoint
$H^{*}$-closed sets $\mathbb{F}_{1}$ and $\mathbb{F}_{2}$, there
exist disjoint $H^{*}$-open sets $\mathbb{U}_{1}$ and
$\mathbb{U}_{2}$ such that
\[
\mathbb{F}_{1}\subseteq\mathbb{U}_{1}
\qquad\text{and}\qquad
\mathbb{F}_{2}\subseteq\mathbb{U}_{2}.
\]
head: environment

label: thm:Hstar-normal-associated
title: Theorem
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Suppose first that $(\mathbb{X},\tau)$ is $H^{*}$-normal. Let
$\mathbb{F}_{1}$ and $\mathbb{F}_{2}$ be disjoint closed subsets of
$(\mathbb{X},\tau_{H^{*}})$. Since the closed sets of
$\tau_{H^{*}}$ are exactly the $H^{*}$-closed sets,
\[
\mathbb{F}_{1},\mathbb{F}_{2}\in H^{*}C(\mathbb{X}).
\]
By $H^{*}$-normality, there exist disjoint $H^{*}$-open sets
$\mathbb{U}_{1}$ and $\mathbb{U}_{2}$ such that
\[
\mathbb{F}_{1}\subseteq\mathbb{U}_{1},
\qquad
\mathbb{F}_{2}\subseteq\mathbb{U}_{2}.
\]
Since
\[
H^{*}O(\mathbb{X})=\tau_{H^{*}},
\]
the sets $\mathbb{U}_{1}$ and $\mathbb{U}_{2}$ are
$\tau_{H^{*}}$-open. Therefore
$(\mathbb{X},\tau_{H^{*}})$ is normal.

Conversely, suppose that $(\mathbb{X},\tau_{H^{*}})$ is normal.
Let
\[
\mathbb{F}_{1},\mathbb{F}_{2}\in H^{*}C(\mathbb{X})
\]
be disjoint. Then $\mathbb{F}_{1}$ and $\mathbb{F}_{2}$ are closed
in $\tau_{H^{*}}$. Hence there exist disjoint
$\tau_{H^{*}}$-open sets $\mathbb{U}_{1}$ and $\mathbb{U}_{2}$
such that
\[
\mathbb{F}_{1}\subseteq\mathbb{U}_{1},
\qquad
\mathbb{F}_{2}\subseteq\mathbb{U}_{2}.
\]
These sets are $H^{*}$-open. Thus
$(\mathbb{X},\tau)$ is $H^{*}$-normal.
head: environment

label: def:Hstar-T4
title: Definition
body_md:
\label{def:Hstar-T4}
The space $(\mathbb{X},\tau)$ is called an
\emph{$H^{*}$-$T_{4}$ space} if it is both $H^{*}$-normal and
$H^{*}$-$T_{1}$.
head: environment

label: cor:Hstar-T4-associated
title: Corollary
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
This follows from
Theorem~\ref{thm:Hstar-normal-associated} and
Theorem~\ref{thm:Hstar-T1-associated}.
head: environment

label: def:Hstar-completely-regular
title: Definition
body_md:
\label{def:Hstar-completely-regular}
A topological space $(\mathbb{X},\tau)$ is said to be
\emph{$H^{*}$-completely regular} if, whenever
$\mathbb{F}\in H^{*}C(\mathbb{X})$ and
$k\in\mathbb{X}\setminus\mathbb{F}$, there exists a function
\[
f:\mathbb{X}\longrightarrow[0,1]
\]
which is continuous from
$(\mathbb{X},\tau_{H^{*}})$ to $[0,1]$ endowed with its usual
topology and satisfies
\[
f(k)=0
\qquad\text{and}\qquad
f(\mathbb{F})=\{1\}.
\]
head: environment

label: thm:Hstar-completely-regular-associated
title: Theorem
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
The $\tau_{H^{*}}$-closed subsets of $\mathbb{X}$ are precisely the
members of $H^{*}C(\mathbb{X})$. Moreover, the continuity required
in Definition~\ref{def:Hstar-completely-regular} is exactly
continuity with respect to $\tau_{H^{*}}$. Therefore the defining
point--closed-set separation condition for $H^{*}$-complete
regularity is identical to the classical complete regularity
condition in $(\mathbb{X},\tau_{H^{*}})$.
head: environment

label: def:Hstar-Tychonoff
title: Definition
head: environment

label: cor:Hstar-Tychonoff-associated
title: Corollary
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
This follows from
Theorem~\ref{thm:Hstar-completely-regular-associated} and
Theorem~\ref{thm:Hstar-T1-associated}.
head: environment

label: thm:Hstar-transfer-principle
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm:Hstar-transfer-principle}
Suppose that
\[
\tau_{H^{*}}=H^{*}O(\mathbb{X})
\]
is an ordinary topology on $\mathbb{X}$. Then every property
formulated exclusively in terms of the members of
$H^{*}O(\mathbb{X})$, their complements, and the corresponding
closure and interior operators admits the equivalent classical
formulation in $(\mathbb{X},\tau_{H^{*}})$.
head: environment
name: Transfer Principle

title: Proof
body_md:
By Definition~\ref{def:associated-Hstar-topology},
\[
\tau_{H^{*}}=H^{*}O(\mathbb{X}).
\]
Thus the open subsets of $(\mathbb{X},\tau_{H^{*}})$ are precisely
the $H^{*}$-open subsets of $\mathbb{X}$. Taking complements shows
that the $\tau_{H^{*}}$-closed sets are precisely the members of
$H^{*}C(\mathbb{X})$.

Furthermore, by
Corollary~\ref{cor:Hstar-associated-closure}, for every
$\mathbb{A}\subseteq\mathbb{X}$,
\[
H^{*}\operatorname{Cl}(\mathbb{A})
=
\operatorname{Cl}_{\tau_{H^{*}}}(\mathbb{A})
\]
and
\[
H^{*}\operatorname{Int}(\mathbb{A})
=
\operatorname{Int}_{\tau_{H^{*}}}(\mathbb{A}).
\]
Consequently, a property expressed solely through these objects has
the same formulation after replacing the $H^{*}$-open,
$H^{*}$-closed, $H^{*}$-closure, and $H^{*}$-interior structures
by their corresponding objects in
$(\mathbb{X},\tau_{H^{*}})$.
head: environment

label: rem:transfer-limitation
title: Remark
body_md:
\label{rem:transfer-limitation}
Theorem~\ref{thm:Hstar-transfer-principle} is an identification
principle and should not be interpreted as asserting that
$(\mathbb{X},\tau_{H^{*}})$ automatically satisfies any particular
classical separation axiom. For example, regularity, complete
regularity, normality, or perfect normality must still be established
from appropriate additional hypotheses.

Likewise, stronger separation conclusions proved for other
generalized-topological constructions cannot be transferred to the
present $H^{*}$-framework merely because
$H^{*}O(\mathbb{X})$ forms a topology. Such conclusions require
their own hypotheses and proofs.
head: environment

label: ex:finite-discrete-Hstar
title: Example
body_md:
\label{ex:finite-discrete-Hstar}
Let
\[
\mathbb{X}=\{k,l,m\}
\]
and consider the topology
\[
\tau=
\left\{
\varnothing,\mathbb{X},\{k,l\}
\right\}.
\]
For this space, every subset of $\mathbb{X}$ is $h$-open as well
as $h$-closed. Consequently,
\[
h\text{-}\operatorname{Cl}(\mathbb{A})=\mathbb{A}
\]
for every $\mathbb{A}\subseteq\mathbb{X}$.

It follows from the definition of an $H^{*}$-closed set that every
subset of $\mathbb{X}$ is $H^{*}$-closed. Hence
\[
H^{*}C(\mathbb{X})=\mathcal{P}(\mathbb{X}),
\]
and, by taking complements,
\[
H^{*}O(\mathbb{X})=\mathcal{P}(\mathbb{X}).
\]
Therefore,
\[
\tau_{H^{*}}
=
H^{*}O(\mathbb{X})
=
\mathcal{P}(\mathbb{X}),
\]
which is the discrete topology on $\mathbb{X}$.
head: environment

label: prop:finite-example-separation
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{prop:finite-example-separation}
For the space in Example~\ref{ex:finite-discrete-Hstar},
$(\mathbb{X},\tau_{H^{*}})$ is $T_{0}$, $T_{1}$, Hausdorff,
regular, completely regular, and normal.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Since
\[
\tau_{H^{*}}=\mathcal{P}(\mathbb{X}),
\]
the associated space is discrete. Hence every subset of
$\mathbb{X}$ is both open and closed. The asserted separation
properties follow from the corresponding standard properties of a
discrete topological space.
head: environment

label: prop:finite-original-not-T0
title: Proposition
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Consider the distinct points $k,l\in\mathbb{X}$. The only nonempty
proper open set is
\[
\{k,l\},
\]
which contains both $k$ and $l$. Thus there is no open set in
$\tau$ containing exactly one of these two points. Therefore
$(\mathbb{X},\tau)$ is not $T_{0}$.
head: environment

label: rem:finite-separation-improvement
title: Remark
body_md:
\label{rem:finite-separation-improvement}
Example~\ref{ex:finite-discrete-Hstar} shows that the separation
properties of the associated $H^{*}$-topology need not reflect
those of the original topology. Indeed,
\[
(\mathbb{X},\tau)\text{ is not }T_{0},
\]
whereas
\[
(\mathbb{X},\tau_{H^{*}})
\]
is discrete.

In view of
Corollary~\ref{cor:Hstar-Ti-associated}, the original
$H^{*}$-structure is therefore $H^{*}$-$T_{0}$,
$H^{*}$-$T_{1}$, and $H^{*}$-$T_{2}$, even though the original
topology $\tau$ is not $T_{0}$.
head: environment

label: ex:infinite-discrete-Hstar
title: Example
body_md:
\label{ex:infinite-discrete-Hstar}
Let $\mathbb{A}$ be a set with
\[
|\mathbb{A}|\geq 2,
\]
let $p\notin\mathbb{A}$, and put
\[
\mathbb{X}=\mathbb{A}\cup\{p\}.
\]
Consider the topology
\[
\tau=
\left\{
\varnothing,\mathbb{A},\mathbb{X}
\right\}.
\]

For this space, every subset of $\mathbb{X}$ is $h$-open and
$h$-closed. Consequently,
\[
h\text{-}\operatorname{Cl}(\mathbb{B})=\mathbb{B}
\]
for every $\mathbb{B}\subseteq\mathbb{X}$.

It follows from the defining condition of $H^{*}$-closed sets that
every subset of $\mathbb{X}$ is $H^{*}$-closed. Therefore,
\[
H^{*}C(\mathbb{X})
=
\mathcal{P}(\mathbb{X})
\]
and hence
\[
H^{*}O(\mathbb{X})
=
\mathcal{P}(\mathbb{X}).
\]
Thus
\[
\tau_{H^{*}}
=
\mathcal{P}(\mathbb{X}),
\]
so the associated $H^{*}$-topology is discrete.
head: environment

label: prop:infinite-original-not-T0
title: Proposition
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Since $|\mathbb{A}|\geq2$, choose distinct points
$k,l\in\mathbb{A}$. The only open sets containing either of these
points are
\[
\mathbb{A}
\qquad\text{and}\qquad
\mathbb{X},
\]
and both contain $k$ and $l$. Hence no open set contains exactly
one of these two points. Therefore
$(\mathbb{X},\tau)$ is not $T_{0}$.
head: environment

label: cor:infinite-Hstar-separation
title: Corollary
body_md:
\label{cor:infinite-Hstar-separation}
For the space in Example~\ref{ex:infinite-discrete-Hstar},
$(\mathbb{X},\tau_{H^{*}})$ is $T_{0}$, $T_{1}$, Hausdorff,
regular, completely regular, and normal.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Since
\[
\tau_{H^{*}}=\mathcal{P}(\mathbb{X}),
\]
the associated space is discrete, and the conclusion follows.
head: environment

label: rem:infinite-Hstar-separation
title: Remark
body_md:
\label{rem:infinite-Hstar-separation}
By the correspondence established in
Section~\ref{sec:separation} and
Section~\ref{sec:higher-separation}, the space
$(\mathbb{X},\tau)$ in
Example~\ref{ex:infinite-discrete-Hstar} satisfies the corresponding
$H^{*}$-separation conditions, although its original topology is not
even $T_{0}$.
head: environment

label: prop:tau-subset-Hstar
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{prop:tau-subset-Hstar}
Suppose that every open subset of $(\mathbb{X},\tau)$ is
$H^{*}$-open and that $H^{*}O(\mathbb{X})$ forms an ordinary
topology. Then
\[
\tau\subseteq\tau_{H^{*}}.
\]
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Let $\mathbb{U}\in\tau$. By hypothesis,
$\mathbb{U}\in H^{*}O(\mathbb{X})$. Since
\[
\tau_{H^{*}}=H^{*}O(\mathbb{X}),
\]
we have
\[
\mathbb{U}\in\tau_{H^{*}}.
\]
Therefore,
\[
\tau\subseteq\tau_{H^{*}}.
\]
head: environment

label: rem:Hstar-finer
title: Remark
body_md:
\label{rem:Hstar-finer}
Under the hypotheses of
Proposition~\ref{prop:tau-subset-Hstar}, the associated topology
$\tau_{H^{*}}$ is finer than the original topology $\tau$.
The inclusion may be strict. Indeed, in
Examples~\ref{ex:finite-discrete-Hstar} and
\ref{ex:infinite-discrete-Hstar},
\[
\tau\subsetneq\tau_{H^{*}}
=
\mathcal{P}(\mathbb{X}).
\]
Thus the associated $H^{*}$-topology may contain substantially more
open sets than the original topology.
head: environment

label: prop:separation-transfer-original
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{prop:separation-transfer-original}
Assume that the associated topology $\tau_{H^{*}}$ exists and that
\[
\tau\subseteq\tau_{H^{*}}.
\]
Then:
\[
(\mathbb{X},\tau)\text{ is }T_{0}
\quad\Longrightarrow\quad
(\mathbb{X},\tau)\text{ is }H^{*}\text{-}T_{0},
\]
\[
(\mathbb{X},\tau)\text{ is }T_{1}
\quad\Longrightarrow\quad
(\mathbb{X},\tau)\text{ is }H^{*}\text{-}T_{1},
\]
and
\[
(\mathbb{X},\tau)\text{ is }T_{2}
\quad\Longrightarrow\quad
(\mathbb{X},\tau)\text{ is }H^{*}\text{-}T_{2}.
\]
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Suppose that $(\mathbb{X},\tau)$ satisfies one of the separation
axioms $T_{0}$, $T_{1}$, or $T_{2}$. The open sets required by the
corresponding separation condition belong to $\tau$. Since
\[
\tau\subseteq\tau_{H^{*}}
=
H^{*}O(\mathbb{X}),
\]
the same sets are $H^{*}$-open. Hence the corresponding
$H^{*}$-separation condition follows.
head: environment

label: rem:converse-separation-fails
title: Remark
body_md:
\label{rem:converse-separation-fails}
None of the converse implications in
Proposition~\ref{prop:separation-transfer-original} holds in
general. Indeed, in both
Examples~\ref{ex:finite-discrete-Hstar} and
\ref{ex:infinite-discrete-Hstar}, the original topology is not
$T_{0}$, whereas
\[
\tau_{H^{*}}=\mathcal{P}(\mathbb{X}).
\]
Hence, by
Corollary~\ref{cor:Hstar-Ti-associated}, the corresponding
$H^{*}$-structure is $H^{*}$-$T_{0}$,
$H^{*}$-$T_{1}$, and $H^{*}$-$T_{2}$.
head: environment

label: rem:finer-topology-limitation
title: Remark
body_md:
\label{rem:finer-topology-limitation}
The inclusion
\[
\tau\subseteq\tau_{H^{*}}
\]
should not be used to infer analogous implications for arbitrary
higher separation properties. In particular, regularity, complete
regularity, and normality are not transferred merely from the fact
that one topology is finer than another. Such properties must be
verified independently or through the associated-topology
correspondences established in
Section~\ref{sec:higher-separation}.
head: environment

label: def:Hstar-compact
title: Definition
body_md:
\label{def:Hstar-compact}
A subset $\mathbb{K}\subseteq\mathbb{X}$ is said to be
\emph{$H^{*}$-compact} if every cover of $\mathbb{K}$ by
$H^{*}$-open subsets of $\mathbb{X}$ admits a finite subcover.

In particular, $(\mathbb{X},\tau)$ is called
\emph{$H^{*}$-compact} if $\mathbb{X}$ is $H^{*}$-compact.
head: environment

label: thm:Hstar-compact-associated
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm:Hstar-compact-associated}
Suppose that
\[
\tau_{H^{*}}=H^{*}O(\mathbb{X})
\]
is an ordinary topology on $\mathbb{X}$. Then, for every
$\mathbb{K}\subseteq\mathbb{X}$,
\[
\mathbb{K}\text{ is $H^{*}$-compact}
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
\mathbb{K}\text{ is compact as a subspace of }
(\mathbb{X},\tau_{H^{*}}).
\]
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Suppose first that $\mathbb{K}$ is $H^{*}$-compact. Let
\[
\{\mathbb{U}_{\lambda}:\lambda\in\Lambda\}
\]
be a family of $\tau_{H^{*}}$-open subsets of $\mathbb{X}$ covering
$\mathbb{K}$. Since
\[
\tau_{H^{*}}=H^{*}O(\mathbb{X}),
\]
every $\mathbb{U}_{\lambda}$ is $H^{*}$-open. By
$H^{*}$-compactness, there exist
$\lambda_{1},\ldots,\lambda_{n}\in\Lambda$ such that
\[
\mathbb{K}
\subseteq
\bigcup_{i=1}^{n}\mathbb{U}_{\lambda_i}.
\]
Hence $\mathbb{K}$ is compact in the subspace topology inherited
from $\tau_{H^{*}}$.

Conversely, suppose that $\mathbb{K}$ is compact as a subspace of
$(\mathbb{X},\tau_{H^{*}})$. Let
\[
\{\mathbb{V}_{\mu}:\mu\in M\}
\]
be an $H^{*}$-open cover of $\mathbb{K}$. Since every
$H^{*}$-open set belongs to $\tau_{H^{*}}$, this is a
$\tau_{H^{*}}$-open cover of $\mathbb{K}$. Compactness yields a
finite subcover. Therefore $\mathbb{K}$ is $H^{*}$-compact.
head: environment

label: cor:Hstar-space-compact-associated
title: Corollary
body_md:
\label{cor:Hstar-space-compact-associated}
Suppose that $\tau_{H^{*}}$ is an ordinary topology. Then
\[
(\mathbb{X},\tau)\text{ is $H^{*}$-compact}
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
(\mathbb{X},\tau_{H^{*}})\text{ is compact}.
\]
head: environment

label: thm:Hstar-compact-closed
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm:Hstar-compact-closed}
Suppose that
\[
\tau_{H^{*}}=H^{*}O(\mathbb{X})
\]
is an ordinary topology. If $(\mathbb{X},\tau)$ is
$H^{*}$-$T_{2}$ and
$\mathbb{K}\subseteq\mathbb{X}$ is $H^{*}$-compact, then
$\mathbb{K}$ is $H^{*}$-closed.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
By Theorem~\ref{thm:Hstar-T2-associated},
$(\mathbb{X},\tau_{H^{*}})$ is Hausdorff. Moreover, by
Theorem~\ref{thm:Hstar-compact-associated}, $\mathbb{K}$ is compact
in $(\mathbb{X},\tau_{H^{*}})$.

Every compact subset of a Hausdorff space is closed. Hence
$\mathbb{K}$ is $\tau_{H^{*}}$-closed. Since the closed subsets of
$(\mathbb{X},\tau_{H^{*}})$ are precisely the $H^{*}$-closed
subsets of $\mathbb{X}$,
\[
\mathbb{K}\in H^{*}C(\mathbb{X}).
\]
Therefore $\mathbb{K}$ is $H^{*}$-closed.
head: environment

label: cor:Hstar-compact-singletons
title: Corollary
body_md:
\label{cor:Hstar-compact-singletons}
Suppose that $\tau_{H^{*}}$ is an ordinary topology and
$(\mathbb{X},\tau)$ is $H^{*}$-$T_{2}$. Then every finite subset
of $\mathbb{X}$ is $H^{*}$-closed.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Every finite subset of a topological space is compact. Therefore,
by Theorem~\ref{thm:Hstar-compact-associated}, every finite subset
of $\mathbb{X}$ is $H^{*}$-compact. The conclusion follows from
Theorem~\ref{thm:Hstar-compact-closed}.
head: environment

label: prop:Hstar-compact-implies-original
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{prop:Hstar-compact-implies-original}
Suppose that the associated topology $\tau_{H^{*}}$ exists and
\[
\tau\subseteq\tau_{H^{*}}.
\]
If $\mathbb{K}\subseteq\mathbb{X}$ is $H^{*}$-compact, then
$\mathbb{K}$ is compact with respect to the original topology
$\tau$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Let
\[
\{\mathbb{U}_{\lambda}:\lambda\in\Lambda\}
\]
be a $\tau$-open cover of $\mathbb{K}$. Since
\[
\tau\subseteq\tau_{H^{*}}
=
H^{*}O(\mathbb{X}),
\]
every $\mathbb{U}_{\lambda}$ is $H^{*}$-open. Thus the given family
is an $H^{*}$-open cover of $\mathbb{K}$.

By $H^{*}$-compactness, it admits a finite subcover. Hence
$\mathbb{K}$ is compact in the topology $\tau$.
head: environment

label: rem:compactness-converse
title: Remark
body_md:
\label{rem:compactness-converse}
The converse of
Proposition~\ref{prop:Hstar-compact-implies-original} does not
follow merely from
\[
\tau\subseteq\tau_{H^{*}}.
\]
Passing from $\tau$ to the finer topology $\tau_{H^{*}}$ may
introduce additional open covers. Consequently, compactness with
respect to $\tau$ does not in general imply compactness with respect
to $\tau_{H^{*}}$.
head: environment

label: prop:equal-topologies-compactness
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{prop:equal-topologies-compactness}
If
\[
\tau=\tau_{H^{*}},
\]
then, for every $\mathbb{K}\subseteq\mathbb{X}$,
\[
\mathbb{K}\text{ is compact in }(\mathbb{X},\tau)
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
\mathbb{K}\text{ is $H^{*}$-compact}.
\]
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
If
\[
\tau=\tau_{H^{*}}=H^{*}O(\mathbb{X}),
\]
then the $\tau$-open covers of $\mathbb{K}$ are exactly its
$H^{*}$-open covers. Hence the two compactness conditions coincide.
head: environment

label: prop:discrete-Hstar-compact
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{prop:discrete-Hstar-compact}
Suppose that
\[
\tau_{H^{*}}=\mathcal{P}(\mathbb{X}).
\]
Then, for every $\mathbb{K}\subseteq\mathbb{X}$,
\[
\mathbb{K}\text{ is $H^{*}$-compact}
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
\mathbb{K}\text{ is finite}.
\]
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Since
\[
\tau_{H^{*}}=\mathcal{P}(\mathbb{X}),
\]
the associated space is discrete. By
Theorem~\ref{thm:Hstar-compact-associated},
$H^{*}$-compactness of $\mathbb{K}$ is equivalent to compactness of
$\mathbb{K}$ in the associated discrete topology.

If $\mathbb{K}$ is finite, then it is compact.

Conversely, suppose that $\mathbb{K}$ is infinite. The family
\[
\bigl\{\{k\}:k\in\mathbb{K}\bigr\}
\]
is an open cover of $\mathbb{K}$ in the discrete topology. No finite
subfamily covers $\mathbb{K}$. Thus $\mathbb{K}$ is not compact and
hence is not $H^{*}$-compact.

Therefore,
\[
\mathbb{K}\text{ is $H^{*}$-compact}
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
\mathbb{K}\text{ is finite}.
\]
head: environment

label: cor:infinite-discrete-not-Hstar-compact
title: Corollary
body_md:
\label{cor:infinite-discrete-not-Hstar-compact}
If $\mathbb{X}$ is infinite and
\[
\tau_{H^{*}}=\mathcal{P}(\mathbb{X}),
\]
then $(\mathbb{X},\tau)$ is not $H^{*}$-compact.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
By Proposition~\ref{prop:discrete-Hstar-compact},
$\mathbb{X}$ is $H^{*}$-compact if and only if $\mathbb{X}$ is
finite. Hence an infinite $\mathbb{X}$ cannot be
$H^{*}$-compact.
head: environment

label: rem:compactness-separation-tradeoff
title: Remark
body_md:
\label{rem:compactness-separation-tradeoff}
The discrete examples illustrate that the passage to the associated
$H^{*}$-topology may have different effects on separation and
compactness. In the examples of Section~\ref{sec:examples}, the
associated topology is discrete and therefore satisfies strong
separation properties. If the underlying set is infinite, however,
the same discrete associated topology is not compact. Thus improved
separation behaviour of the associated topology does not imply
compactness.
head: environment

label: def:Hstar-irresolute
title: Definition
body_md:
\label{def:Hstar-irresolute}
A mapping
\[
f:(\mathbb{X},\tau)\longrightarrow(\mathbb{Y},\sigma)
\]
is called \emph{$H^{*}$-irresolute} if
\[
f^{-1}(\mathbb{V})\in H^{*}O(\mathbb{X})
\]
for every
\[
\mathbb{V}\in H^{*}O(\mathbb{Y}).
\]
head: environment

label: thm:Hstar-irresolute-continuous
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm:Hstar-irresolute-continuous}
Suppose that
\[
\tau_{H^{*}}=H^{*}O(\mathbb{X})
\qquad\text{and}\qquad
\sigma_{H^{*}}=H^{*}O(\mathbb{Y})
\]
are ordinary topologies. Then a mapping
\[
f:(\mathbb{X},\tau)\longrightarrow(\mathbb{Y},\sigma)
\]
is $H^{*}$-irresolute if and only if
\[
f:(\mathbb{X},\tau_{H^{*}})
\longrightarrow
(\mathbb{Y},\sigma_{H^{*}})
\]
is continuous.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Suppose that $f$ is $H^{*}$-irresolute. Let
\[
\mathbb{V}\in\sigma_{H^{*}}.
\]
Since
\[
\sigma_{H^{*}}=H^{*}O(\mathbb{Y}),
\]
the set $\mathbb{V}$ is $H^{*}$-open in $\mathbb{Y}$. Therefore,
by $H^{*}$-irresoluteness,
\[
f^{-1}(\mathbb{V})\in H^{*}O(\mathbb{X})
=\tau_{H^{*}}.
\]
Hence
\[
f:(\mathbb{X},\tau_{H^{*}})
\longrightarrow
(\mathbb{Y},\sigma_{H^{*}})
\]
is continuous.

Conversely, suppose that $f$ is continuous between the associated
topologies. If
\[
\mathbb{V}\in H^{*}O(\mathbb{Y}),
\]
then
\[
\mathbb{V}\in\sigma_{H^{*}}.
\]
Thus
\[
f^{-1}(\mathbb{V})\in\tau_{H^{*}}
=H^{*}O(\mathbb{X}),
\]
and hence $f$ is $H^{*}$-irresolute.
head: environment

label: rem:Hstar-irresolute-associated
title: Remark
body_md:
\label{rem:Hstar-irresolute-associated}
Thus, once the associated topologies exist,
$H^{*}$-irresoluteness is not a separate mapping condition at the
associated-topology level; it is precisely ordinary continuity
between the spaces
\[
(\mathbb{X},\tau_{H^{*}})
\qquad\text{and}\qquad
(\mathbb{Y},\sigma_{H^{*}}).
\]
head: environment

label: thm:inverse-Hstar-D
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm:inverse-Hstar-D}
Let
\[
f:(\mathbb{X},\tau)\longrightarrow(\mathbb{Y},\sigma)
\]
be an $H^{*}$-irresolute surjection. If $\mathbb{D}$ is an
$H^{*}D$-set in $\mathbb{Y}$, then
$f^{-1}(\mathbb{D})$ is an $H^{*}D$-set in $\mathbb{X}$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Let $\mathbb{D}$ be an $H^{*}D$-set in $\mathbb{Y}$. Then there
exist
\[
\mathbb{U},\mathbb{V}\in H^{*}O(\mathbb{Y})
\]
such that
\[
\mathbb{D}=\mathbb{U}\setminus\mathbb{V}
\qquad\text{and}\qquad
\mathbb{U}\neq\mathbb{Y}.
\]
Since $f$ is $H^{*}$-irresolute,
\[
f^{-1}(\mathbb{U}),
\,
f^{-1}(\mathbb{V})
\in H^{*}O(\mathbb{X}).
\]
Furthermore,
\[
\begin{aligned}
f^{-1}(\mathbb{D})
&=
f^{-1}(\mathbb{U}\setminus\mathbb{V})\\
&=
f^{-1}(\mathbb{U})\setminus f^{-1}(\mathbb{V}).
\end{aligned}
\]

It remains to verify the properness condition. Since
$\mathbb{U}\neq\mathbb{Y}$, choose
\[
y\in\mathbb{Y}\setminus\mathbb{U}.
\]
Because $f$ is surjective, there exists $x\in\mathbb{X}$ such that
\[
f(x)=y.
\]
Hence
\[
x\notin f^{-1}(\mathbb{U}),
\]
so that
\[
f^{-1}(\mathbb{U})\neq\mathbb{X}.
\]
Therefore $f^{-1}(\mathbb{D})$ is an $H^{*}D$-set in
$\mathbb{X}$.
head: environment

label: rem:surjectivity-Hstar-D
title: Remark
body_md:
\label{rem:surjectivity-Hstar-D}
The surjectivity assumption in
Theorem~\ref{thm:inverse-Hstar-D} is essential for the preceding
argument. Indeed, from
\[
\mathbb{U}\neq\mathbb{Y}
\]
alone one cannot conclude that
\[
f^{-1}(\mathbb{U})\neq\mathbb{X}.
\]
Surjectivity ensures that a point of
$\mathbb{Y}\setminus\mathbb{U}$ has a preimage in $\mathbb{X}$.
head: environment

label: thm:Hstar-D1-injective
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm:Hstar-D1-injective}
Let
\[
f:(\mathbb{X},\tau)\longrightarrow(\mathbb{Y},\sigma)
\]
be an $H^{*}$-irresolute bijection. If
$(\mathbb{Y},\sigma)$ is $H^{*}$-$D_{1}$, then
$(\mathbb{X},\tau)$ is $H^{*}$-$D_{1}$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Let $k,l\in\mathbb{X}$ with $k\neq l$. Since $f$ is injective,
\[
f(k)\neq f(l).
\]
As $(\mathbb{Y},\sigma)$ is $H^{*}$-$D_{1}$, there exist
$H^{*}D$-sets $\mathbb{D}_{1}$ and $\mathbb{D}_{2}$ in
$\mathbb{Y}$ such that
\[
f(k)\in\mathbb{D}_{1},
\qquad
f(l)\notin\mathbb{D}_{1},
\]
and
\[
f(l)\in\mathbb{D}_{2},
\qquad
f(k)\notin\mathbb{D}_{2}.
\]

Since $f$ is bijective, it is in particular surjective. Hence
Theorem~\ref{thm:inverse-Hstar-D} implies that
\[
f^{-1}(\mathbb{D}_{1})
\quad\text{and}\quad
f^{-1}(\mathbb{D}_{2})
\]
are $H^{*}D$-sets in $\mathbb{X}$. Moreover,
\[
k\in f^{-1}(\mathbb{D}_{1}),
\qquad
l\notin f^{-1}(\mathbb{D}_{1}),
\]
and
\[
l\in f^{-1}(\mathbb{D}_{2}),
\qquad
k\notin f^{-1}(\mathbb{D}_{2}).
\]
Therefore $(\mathbb{X},\tau)$ is $H^{*}$-$D_{1}$.
head: environment

label: thm:Hstar-D2-injective
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm:Hstar-D2-injective}
Let
\[
f:(\mathbb{X},\tau)\longrightarrow(\mathbb{Y},\sigma)
\]
be an $H^{*}$-irresolute bijection. If
$(\mathbb{Y},\sigma)$ is $H^{*}$-$D_{2}$, then
$(\mathbb{X},\tau)$ is $H^{*}$-$D_{2}$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Let $k,l\in\mathbb{X}$ with $k\neq l$. Since $f$ is injective,
\[
f(k)\neq f(l).
\]
By the $H^{*}$-$D_{2}$ property of $\mathbb{Y}$, there exist
disjoint $H^{*}D$-sets $\mathbb{D}_{1}$ and $\mathbb{D}_{2}$ such
that
\[
f(k)\in\mathbb{D}_{1},
\qquad
f(l)\in\mathbb{D}_{2}.
\]

Since $f$ is surjective,
Theorem~\ref{thm:inverse-Hstar-D} shows that
$f^{-1}(\mathbb{D}_{1})$ and
$f^{-1}(\mathbb{D}_{2})$ are $H^{*}D$-sets in $\mathbb{X}$.
Furthermore,
\[
\begin{aligned}
f^{-1}(\mathbb{D}_{1})
\cap
f^{-1}(\mathbb{D}_{2})
&=
f^{-1}(\mathbb{D}_{1}\cap\mathbb{D}_{2})\\
&=
f^{-1}(\varnothing)\\
&=
\varnothing.
\end{aligned}
\]
Also,
\[
k\in f^{-1}(\mathbb{D}_{1}),
\qquad
l\in f^{-1}(\mathbb{D}_{2}).
\]
Therefore $(\mathbb{X},\tau)$ is $H^{*}$-$D_{2}$.
head: environment

label: thm:Hstar-compact-image
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm:Hstar-compact-image}
Suppose that
\[
\tau_{H^{*}}=H^{*}O(\mathbb{X})
\qquad\text{and}\qquad
\sigma_{H^{*}}=H^{*}O(\mathbb{Y})
\]
are ordinary topologies. Let
\[
f:(\mathbb{X},\tau)\longrightarrow(\mathbb{Y},\sigma)
\]
be $H^{*}$-irresolute. If
$\mathbb{K}\subseteq\mathbb{X}$ is $H^{*}$-compact, then
$f(\mathbb{K})$ is $H^{*}$-compact in $\mathbb{Y}$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
By Theorem~\ref{thm:Hstar-irresolute-continuous},
\[
f:(\mathbb{X},\tau_{H^{*}})
\longrightarrow
(\mathbb{Y},\sigma_{H^{*}})
\]
is continuous.

By Theorem~\ref{thm:Hstar-compact-associated},
$\mathbb{K}$ is compact as a subspace of
$(\mathbb{X},\tau_{H^{*}})$. Since continuous images of compact
spaces are compact,
\[
f(\mathbb{K})
\]
is compact as a subspace of
$(\mathbb{Y},\sigma_{H^{*}})$.

Applying Theorem~\ref{thm:Hstar-compact-associated} to
$(\mathbb{Y},\sigma)$, we conclude that $f(\mathbb{K})$ is
$H^{*}$-compact.
head: environment

label: cor:Hstar-compact-surjection
title: Corollary
body_md:
\label{cor:Hstar-compact-surjection}
Suppose that the associated topologies $\tau_{H^{*}}$ and
$\sigma_{H^{*}}$ exist. Let
\[
f:(\mathbb{X},\tau)\longrightarrow(\mathbb{Y},\sigma)
\]
be an $H^{*}$-irresolute surjection. If
$(\mathbb{X},\tau)$ is $H^{*}$-compact, then
$(\mathbb{Y},\sigma)$ is $H^{*}$-compact.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Apply Theorem~\ref{thm:Hstar-compact-image} with
\[
\mathbb{K}=\mathbb{X}.
\]
Since $f$ is surjective,
\[
f(\mathbb{X})=\mathbb{Y}.
\]
Hence $\mathbb{Y}$ is $H^{*}$-compact.
head: environment

label: def:Hstar-homeomorphism
title: Definition
body_md:
\label{def:Hstar-homeomorphism}
A bijection
\[
f:(\mathbb{X},\tau)\longrightarrow(\mathbb{Y},\sigma)
\]
is called an \emph{$H^{*}$-homeomorphism} if both $f$ and
$f^{-1}$ are $H^{*}$-irresolute.
head: environment

label: thm:Hstar-homeomorphism-associated
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm:Hstar-homeomorphism-associated}
Suppose that
\[
\tau_{H^{*}}=H^{*}O(\mathbb{X})
\qquad\text{and}\qquad
\sigma_{H^{*}}=H^{*}O(\mathbb{Y})
\]
are ordinary topologies. Then a bijection
\[
f:(\mathbb{X},\tau)\longrightarrow(\mathbb{Y},\sigma)
\]
is an $H^{*}$-homeomorphism if and only if
\[
f:(\mathbb{X},\tau_{H^{*}})
\longrightarrow
(\mathbb{Y},\sigma_{H^{*}})
\]
is a homeomorphism.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
By Theorem~\ref{thm:Hstar-irresolute-continuous},
$f$ is $H^{*}$-irresolute if and only if
\[
f:(\mathbb{X},\tau_{H^{*}})
\longrightarrow
(\mathbb{Y},\sigma_{H^{*}})
\]
is continuous.

Applying the same theorem to the inverse bijection
\[
f^{-1}:(\mathbb{Y},\sigma)
\longrightarrow
(\mathbb{X},\tau),
\]
we obtain that $f^{-1}$ is $H^{*}$-irresolute if and only if
\[
f^{-1}:(\mathbb{Y},\sigma_{H^{*}})
\longrightarrow
(\mathbb{X},\tau_{H^{*}})
\]
is continuous.

Thus both $f$ and $f^{-1}$ are $H^{*}$-irresolute if and only if
$f$ is a homeomorphism between the associated spaces.
head: environment

label: cor:Hstar-homeomorphic-invariants
title: Corollary
body_md:
\label{cor:Hstar-homeomorphic-invariants}
Suppose that the associated topologies exist. Then every
topological invariant of the associated spaces is preserved under
an $H^{*}$-homeomorphism. In particular, the $H^{*}$-compactness
and $H^{*}$-separation properties identified in the preceding
sections are preserved under $H^{*}$-homeomorphisms.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
By Theorem~\ref{thm:Hstar-homeomorphism-associated}, an
$H^{*}$-homeomorphism is precisely a homeomorphism between the
associated spaces. Hence every topological invariant of those
spaces is preserved.

The assertions concerning $H^{*}$-compactness and the
$H^{*}$-separation properties follow from their corresponding
associated-topology characterizations established in
Sections~\ref{sec:separation}--\ref{sec:compactness}.
head: environment

label: rem:mapping-associated-view
title: Remark
body_md:
\label{rem:mapping-associated-view}
The associated-topology approach therefore provides a unified
interpretation of the mapping theory. Whenever
\[
\tau_{H^{*}}=H^{*}O(\mathbb{X})
\quad\text{and}\quad
\sigma_{H^{*}}=H^{*}O(\mathbb{Y})
\]
are ordinary topologies, $H^{*}$-irresolute mappings are precisely
continuous mappings between the associated spaces, while
$H^{*}$-homeomorphisms are precisely homeomorphisms between them.
Consequently, classical preservation results may be applied whenever
the corresponding $H^{*}$-property has already been identified with
a topological property of the associated space.
head: environment

label: prop:Hstar-generalized-mechanism
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{prop:Hstar-generalized-mechanism}
Suppose that $H^{*}C(\mathbb{X})$ is closed under arbitrary
intersections. Then
\[
\Gamma_{H^{*}}=H^{*}O(\mathbb{X})
\]
is a strong generalized topology on $\mathbb{X}$, and the
$\Gamma_{H^{*}}$-closed sets are precisely the members of
$H^{*}C(\mathbb{X})$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
The first assertion is exactly
Theorem~\ref{thm:Hstar-strong-generalized-topology}. By
Proposition~\ref{prop:Gamma-Hstar-closed}, the complements of the
members of $\Gamma_{H^{*}}$ are precisely the members of
$H^{*}C(\mathbb{X})$. Hence these are exactly the
$\Gamma_{H^{*}}$-closed sets.
head: environment

label: rem:no-automatic-strong-separation
title: Remark
body_md:
\label{rem:no-automatic-strong-separation}
The existence of the strong generalized topology
$\Gamma_{H^{*}}$ does not by itself imply Hausdorffness,
regularity, complete regularity, normality, perfect normality, or
any other stronger separation property. Similarly, even when
$\tau_{H^{*}}$ exists as an ordinary topology, such properties do
not follow merely from its construction.

Accordingly, stronger separation conclusions established for other
generalized-topological or operator-generated structures require
their own hypotheses and cannot be transferred automatically to the
$H^{*}$-generated structure.
head: environment
